utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes Your Honour, this is the case number IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning Your Honours, good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Smith [Continued]:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, whilst you were at the KP Dom, did you ever see anyone being beaten whilst you were inside the administration building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was cleaning the administration building, I saw Asim Mezbur and Nurko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you, in fact, see being beaten? You said you saw Asim Mezbur and Nurko Nisic. Who was being beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nurko Nisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was beating him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where these military police were from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how many military police were beating him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you explain to the Court what they were doing, how they were beating him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were kicking him, they were hitting him with their hands, in order for him to recognise some names, which I couldn't make out because my head was bowed as my colleague and I were cleaning something over there at the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than beating him with their hands, did they use anything else to beat him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which room or which place in the administration building was he being beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the ground floor, in the room for searches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you watching this from, this beating?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the entrance into the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Asim Mezbur was present whilst Nurko was being beaten. What was happening to him whilst Nurko was being beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He stood quietly, facing the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any guards present when Nurko was being beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were present towards their office, the guards office. They were standing on a platform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many guards were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Two or three were standing at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the names of these guards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you continue to watch the beating through until it finished or did you leave before that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there for ten minutes and then one of the guards said that we should be taken to the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst the beating was going on, did the guards try to stop it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the guards take you to the compound during the beating?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He opened the entrance door for me and I entered the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to pass through the searching room to get into the compound?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Half a metre away from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why Nurko Nisic was being beaten on that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly these were the top people. Nurko was president of the municipality; Asim Mezbur was in a prominent position at the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure of Nurko Nisic's position?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but that's what people assumed. That's what people talked about, that he was president of the municipality, the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I would just ask the usher if Prosecution Exhibit 6/1A, the plan of the administration building, be placed on the overhead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you can look at the plan of the KP Dom which is on your screen, it shows the ground floor of the administration building at the bottom of the plan. Does that plan look familiar to you in terms of the layout of the administration building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point out the room that you call the searching room in which Nurko was being beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just use the silver pointer and place it on the screen or the overhead projector that's to the right of you.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the room is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness indicates the room that has the entrance into the KP Dom compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also on the map, could you indicate the place where you were when you were watching this beating. You said it was near the entrance.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The entrance door leading into the searching room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness indicates the entrance to the KP Dom administration building on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that entrance, could you see through to the searching room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I was three or four metres away. A door with bars open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was anyone with you when you were watching this beating, any other detainee?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mujo Dudic was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the diagram, could you show where the guards were in relation to the entrance?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this platform here, by the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness indicates the inside of the entrance to the KP Dom, slightly to the left, near the steps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sorry, which steps? I didn't -- he moved it so quickly I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to the left of the entrance there's some steps, I think about three steps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What's being regarded as the reception room or the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I just ask that the usher show the Witness the following photograph, it's Prosecution Exhibit 18 and it's number 7446.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, looking at this photograph, is that familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does that photograph show?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows the lower iron door entering the compound, the platform where three guards stood, and their office where the guards were, the reception office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You can see the steps actually, I had never noticed that before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these are the three guards that you mentioned were present when the beating was occurring?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Three guards were on the platform while they were beaten by the military police inside, in the searching room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how many metres from where Nurko was being beaten were these guards, these three guards on the platform?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about the same; three or four metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I can ask that the usher show the witness the photograph from P18, photograph 7469 and 7470. Witness, looking at the top photograph, is this familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entrance door leading into the searching room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you standing in relation to the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right by the entrance into the searching room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The witness indicates with the pointer at the bottom middle of the photograph, just before the entrance to the searching room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you can now look at the photograph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can now look at the photograph 7470, is that familiar to you, that photograph?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does that show?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the searching room that we all had to pass through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you point in that photograph where Nurko Nisic was being beaten on that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Nurko stood there and Asim Mezbur stood somewhere around here. They were right next to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness indicates the left-hand side of the photograph, in front of the water heater on the wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which way was Nurko Nisic facing when he was being beaten? Was he facing the wall or away from it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both were facing the wall and their hands were on the wall, by the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Nurko was being beaten, was he being beaten -- did he fall to the ground or did he stay standing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was present there, he was on his feet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that during the beating, a guard took you through into the compound. Can you indicate the door on the photograph, the lower photograph, that you were taken through?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, the witness indicates the door with the arrow alongside of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: We are finished with those photographs, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the day that Nurko Nisic was being beaten in the searching room, what room were you detained in, what room did you sleep in at that time? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were sleeping in Room 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what room was Nurko Nisic sleeping in at that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure which room he slept in, but Asim Mezbur slept in the same room that I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear sounds of Nurko Nisic being beaten on any other occasion other than the day that you saw him being beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps just going back to the day that he was beaten, about what month and what year did that occur?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1992, mid-May, June. That's when all the beatings took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said that you heard Nurko being beaten on another occasion. When did that occur?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later, after that, in the evening hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the beating that you actually saw of Nurko, was that in the daytime hours or in the evening?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day; 12.00, 12.30, it was lunchtime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when Nurko was being beaten during that daytime that you saw, did you hear him say anything or scream or moan?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear Nurko Nisic being beaten on the same day that you saw him being beaten, or was it on another day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about what month was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think all of that was mid-May, June. All of that happened then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say that you heard him being beaten in the evening hours, was it during the light or when it was dark?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in the early evening hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this other occasion that you heard Nurko Nisic being beaten, where were you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Room 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you hear the sounds of Nurko Nisic being beaten coming from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in Room 11 then because people were taken out regularly. That is to say that we were all by the window. That's when Nurko Nisic was beaten, most probably, because one of the guards was yelling, "Get up, Nurko, that's no way to defend Bosnia." He was losing consciousness. You could hear buckets of water being thrown on him and we knew that it was Nurko Nisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any sounds of beating coming from that place?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beating. His screams. Hitting buckets against the wall; most probably they were pouring water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did this beating go on for?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this particular beating, did you see Nurko Nisic again?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did the sounds of this beating come from? What building, what floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ground floor. We knew where Room 11 was, that is to say, between the toilet and the staircase that went upstairs. The second or third window, we were not sure which one out of those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just ask that the usher show the witness Prosecution Exhibit 18 and photograph number 07474.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the photograph that's on the screen is a photograph of the administration building on the left-hand side, and the far left-hand corner of the photograph is the corner of the administration building to where the main entrance door to the administration building is located. Is that building familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very familiar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show with the pointer on the photograph the window that you heard the sounds of this beating coming from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's this window, behind the drainpipe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness indicates the fourth window from the right on the ground floor of the administration building, just immediately to the right of the drainpipe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you mean the first drainpipe. I think that might be a second drainpipe at the end of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct. Your Honour, just to be clear, the first full drainpipe that goes to the top of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, whilst you were at the KP Dom, did you ever see dead human bodies stranded in the Drina river?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you see these bodies stranded in relation to the front entrance of the KP Dom? Was it to the right or to the left in the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the right down the KP Dom on the bank, on a little island that was on the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that on the Gorazde side of the bridge in front of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how far from the bridge did you see these bodies stranded?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately 50 to 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on about how many occasions did you see bodies stranded in the river?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure; four or five times, at least, in the afternoon hours, because the level of water goes down then and then this would remain on the banks of the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how was it that you got to see these bodies in the Drina River? You mentioned that you were detained at the KP Dom. How was it that you were able to get out of the KP Dom and see these bodies?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guard took me out. He would take four or five of us men out. We would push them down the Drina and go back to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do this on about four or five occasions?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of those four or five occasions, in total, about how many bodies did you push down the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four bodies, I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these bodies men or women?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men. There was also some cattle that was left there, so all of this was flowing down the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these men in civilian or military clothes; did you take any notice?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these men of varying ages or were they of one particular age?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Older people, from the age of 50 onwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time period did you see these bodies in the river? In what months were you asked to go out and push them further into the river?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The month of May, the month of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which guard asked you to do this?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Burilo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he work at the KP Dom for the whole time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Otherwise, he was in charge of the work units, taking them out. He was a guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the first occasion that you saw a human body in the Drina River and you pushed it further into the river, what were you asked by Burilo, what were you asked to do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All that could be reached, we were supposed to push further down the Drina. Before us, two or three men had got out. There were two cows and one sheep on the bank, the same level as that islet in the river, and we pushed them further away down the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you left the KP Dom and were taken out towards the river, were you told that you were, in fact, going to be doing that, pushing the bodies down the river, or did you not know what you would be doing when you got to the river?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know until I got outside, through the gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told by Burilo what you were going to do after you left the gate, or was it only until you got to the river that you found out what you had to do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we got out through the gate, he gave us some sticks or planks and told us what we were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this before you saw the first body in the river?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Burilo tell you where these bodies had actually come from, whether they were from the KP Dom or from some other place?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, are you going to ask whether he recognised any of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I was just going to do that now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the bodies, any of the four or five that you moved?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many other detainees were with you when you were asked to push these bodies in the river on these occasions?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a small unit which did the job all the time. There was me, Mujo Dudic and Kelta Mandzo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whilst you pushed these bodies further into the river, did Burilo guard you whilst you did this?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was Burilo and there were two guards on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know the names of these two other guards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just ask that a map be placed before the witness, it's Prosecution Exhibit 9/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, looking at this map, do you see the KP Dom in the centre of it, with the number 7 alongside of it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point on the map the location that you --

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KP Dom is this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point on the map the location that these bodies were stranded.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This small peninsula or, rather, islet here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, do we know in the evidence which way the river flows? I think we've had some evidence of this in a previous case, but have we got it in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour; it flows upwards, up the left, towards Gorazde, and you'll see a small arrow alongside the island where the bodies were stranded, showing the direction of the river flowing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You have better eyes than I have, I'm afraid

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Only with these glasses, Your Honour. We've finished with the map now. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask anyone at the KP Dom, or Burilo in particular, as to where these bodies had come from and why you had to do this?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't dare nor was it allowed to talk to the guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you first arrived at the KP Dom, did you find out who the warden was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the outset, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you first find out who the warden of the KP Dom was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt from civilian cooks who worked in the kitchen then, in the same kitchen where I worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they say who the warden was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was cleaning up tables at the time, Savo Todovic would usually come to breakfast, together with the warden and Mitar Rasevic. The three of them were usually come together. I worked in the canteen then; cleaned up tables and did other work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that the cooks, you learned from the cooks who the warden was. Did they say anything to you as to who he was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was to learn who the warden was only later. I didn't know it at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you find out who the warden was later?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out when I worked on his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you work on Milorad Krnojelac's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date. I think it was sometime in November 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who asked you to work on his house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guard who called me out and told me to get ready said I had to go to the warden's house, the house of Mr. Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for about how many days did you work on his house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked with intervals, not every day, that is, but on balance, it was for about 10 days that I worked there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you worked on Krnojelac's house, were other detainees working on it at the same time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were another 10 people who worked there and they worked longer than I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you look at the sheet in front of you, without saying the person's name, did number 73, did he work on the house on some occasions with you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were the other detainees, or some of the other detainees that worked on the house whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 144 worked at that time, then Mustafa Telo, Aziz Telo, there were other people as well whom I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the days that you worked on the house, did the same people work on it every day or did the people change?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the job required, but it was mostly the same people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got to the house in November, had detainees been working on the house prior to your first day of work there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who worked before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got to the house on the first day, what damage did you notice had occurred to it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That house was about 100 per cent devastated, burned down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the walls still standing on the house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no roof, the entire roofing was destroyed. The walls were half destroyed. The facade remained to some extent, remained standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the 10 days, the 10 or so days that you worked on the house, what particular work did you do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were supposed to clean up, scrape off the old paint, and prepare surfaces for cladding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what hours did you work on the house? What time did you start and what time did you finish?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would go out sometime after breakfast, around 7.30 or 8.00, and we would return just before dinner, around 5.00, 5.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how would you get to the house from the KP Dom; who would take you there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Black Mariah would take us there from the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that a type of car?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a closed vehicle, used for the transportation of detainees, prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you go with a guard from the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he would go with us up to the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would the guard, that particular guard, would he stay for the entire day or would he return to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times he did go back because we would be guarded by his son who would be with us the whole day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned "his son"; do you mean Milorad Krnojelac's son?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the first name of his son?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know that he was the elder or the eldest but I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how old was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was around 30, 35 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what would he wear? Would he be in civilian clothing or military clothing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wore the military camouflage uniform. He would -- he appeared in it several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you eat whilst you were at the house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They brought food, much better, much more nutritious food than we had at the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who would cook the food or bring the food to you at the house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His son brought it, his mother, and then the warden would also come occasionally. He came several times to see us, to see how the -- our work is progressing and to see whether any more material is needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you mentioned the son's mother, do you mean Milorad Krnojelac's wife?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Krnojelac's wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that Milorad Krnojelac would come to the house on several occasions. Of the 10 days, the 10 or so days that you worked there, about how many times did he come?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you precisely, but in the evening hours, when we would be returning, he would be with us in the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the transcript says that "he would be with us in the compound" whereas the witness actually said he was with them at the house when they would be returning to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said. He would be waiting with us for the Black Mariah which was supposed to take us to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that clears it up, thank you. Perhaps I should say this to the witness: Sir, everything that you are saying is being translated into both English and French. The interpreters work about half a sentence behind you. When you came in to explain that, for which we are very grateful, you nevertheless interfered with the interpretation of what Mr. Bakrac, the counsel for the Defence, had been telling us. So please, whenever you are asked a question, do pause to enable the interpreters to catch up. Yes, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that Mr. Krnojelac would come to the house to see how the work was progressing and what material was needed. Can you provide a few more details as to the types of things that he would ask the detainees or inquire into in relation to the work on the house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this question directed to me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct. You mentioned that he would inquire about the materials needed and the progress of the house. What type of inquiries did he make?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment while we were waiting for the Black Mariah, we would be making a list of materials needed. Once the Black Mariah wasn't coming for some time --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me. The interpreter would like the witness to start all over again, more slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Witness, perhaps if I can ask you that question again because you are speaking fairly fast and the translators haven't been able to translate it in time. So if I can ask you the question again: What type of inquiries did he make in relation to the materials needed for the house and the progress of the house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would ask us to give him a list of materials needed - how much cement, how many bricks - so that it could be prepared for the next day so that we could continue the work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst Milorad Krnojelac was at the house, did you ever complain to him or any of the other detainees about the conditions at the KP Dom and concerns about your fate there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because he knew, himself, what the situation at the KP Dom was like. He couldn't help much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On one occasion, did Mr. Krnojelac ever state about what he was trying to do for the detainees at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion, we were waiting for the car to arrive to pick us up, and we were talking, and he says, "I can't do much. I'm trying to help you survive although many things are running out of my control. The food is awful, I know that, but we don't get much better."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything along the lines of if it wasn't for him, you all would have been killed?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a leading question. The Prosecutor is putting things into the witness's mouth. The Prosecutor asked the witness to say what Krnojelac said and now the Prosecutor is asking a different question, practically saying to the witness what he should answer. We have the answer before this where the witness said precisely what the accused had told him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: For once, Mr. Bakrac, I agree with you; it is a leading question. Yes, Mr. Smith, it's clearly leading. There's no suggestion that the witness has said that earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't agree if what Mr. Bakrac was saying, that the answer he'd given was intended to be a complete one of everything which was said, but you can't put that to him. You'll have to ask him what was said. The value of what he says now, unfortunately, will be somewhat destroyed, but you'd better go ahead and do it properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did the -- did Mr. Krnojelac say anything further about how he was -- excuse me one moment, Your Honour. Witness, you said that Mr. Krnojelac said he couldn't do much. Did he explain any further as to why he couldn't do much for the detainees Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the rest were orders from the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he say who the command was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what prompted him to say this? Was a question asked of him by the detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably it was some sort of conversation where this issue came up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the conversation, did he state what his role was at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but we drew our own conclusions when he said, "As long as I am warden, nothing will happen to you." We knew as soon as we heard that what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when Milorad Krnojelac was at the house on the number of occasions that you mentioned, how did he treat the detainees there generally?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was good. He acted naturally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on every occasion that you were taken to Krnojelac's house, did you always go in the same vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other vehicle would you go in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I went, I went after this work unit on another job. I was driven by the warden in a car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were driven by the warden, did you have any conversation with him on the way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never got involved in conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why were you driven by Mr. Krnojelac on that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I had left the KP Dom on a special job, a separate job. It was not particularly difficult, but it needed to be done. And it was also on the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get paid for working on Mr. Krnojelac's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you finish working on his house; about what month?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly. I was there for about 10 days. Other people remained there for two months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just going back to when Mr. Krnojelac said to you, "As long as I am the warden, nothing will happen to you," and you said when he said that, you knew what the situation was. What was the situation? What did you understand that to be?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the state of war, I knew what my position was. I knew why I was there. The food was awful. Everybody was just trying to stay alive. So I worked, and I wasn't choosey. I wanted to get out just in order to get some more and better food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were at the KP Dom, did anyone attempt to escape?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Muhamed Zekovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that's the person's first name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called him Zeka. We often used nicknames, so it is very, very hard for me to remember his first name. We called him Zeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember when he attempted to escape; in what year?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1993, July, beginning of August. I'm not sure about the dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he caught and brought back to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After he attempted to escape, were you ever warned about escaping or making any further attempts to escape, any of the detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is to say, that morning, we were lined up in the compound. They brought Zeka and we were deprived of meals and we were forbidden to work for the next 12 or 13 days. That is to say, I did not have any lunch, and I did not have any dinner. Meals were halved, at least, during those 10 days while I was in the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that your --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that when you were lined up and you were warned, who warned you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly. Savo Todovic was there, Rasevic and the warden. They brought him into the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the attempted escape of Zekovic, did the wardens change at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not sure then yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some time after the escape, did the wardens change?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, yes, because that's when the conditions started getting better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you left the KP Dom in October 1994, there was a new warden at that stage; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoran. I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that the conditions started to get better after the wardens changed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what way did the conditions get better? Say, perhaps, in relation to the food first.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had somewhat better food, of better quality. The bed linen was changed every 10 days. I could take a bath every 10 or 15 days. To put it simply, our life was quite different. People were not taken away. We were not beaten. We were registered with the International Red Cross, so the conditions were very good, compared to 1992. We called 1994 our golden year in comparison to 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the wardens changed at the KP Dom, was there more freedom of movement within the compound?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a work unit that went out. There were people who were in rooms then, and they could move about the compound, the yard, they could take a walk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the behaviour of the guards? Did that stay the same, did that improve, or get worse?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an abrupt change. We could not believe it ourselves. We could not believe what was going on. The guards were much softer. You could talk. You could reach agreement with them. We worked together so life became more bearable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that after the warden changed, the bed linen was changed every 10 days. When Krnojelac was the warden, how often was the linen changed on the beds?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. In 1992, I doubt that the bed linen was ever changed until the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1992, how often were you able to take a bath, wash, or shower?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that 1992 period, were detainees able to move about their rooms -- sorry, move about the compound of the KP Dom, outside of their rooms?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no way. We didn't dare go to the window, let alone take a walk, except for the work units that went out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before you arrived at the KP Dom, did you know Mr. Krnojelac, the person that you said was warden?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him because he was a teacher of mathematics in the Veselin Maslesa school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And other than the times that you saw Mr. Krnojelac in the canteen and whilst you were working on his house, did you see him in the compound during 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would see him in the compound. I would see him outside the compound. Usually he'd be at the entrance. Because I was passing to the metal shop so I would see him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who would you see him with? Would you see him with anyone else during this time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually there was Savo Todovic, Mitar Rasevic and Krnojelac who were together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how often would you see Mr. Krnojelac with either one or two of these people?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you exactly. A few times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Krnojelac have a secretary whilst he was at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what date were you released from the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of October 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the two and a half years that you were at the KP Dom, did that affect you in any way psychologically?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took me back a lot. I lost a lot in terms of my life. My psyche is -- I was imprisoned for two and a half years and I didn't share much. I kept so many things within and therefore I did not really communicate with the warden or Savo Todovic, only officially if it had to do with business. That's all the talking I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Bakrac. Cross-examined by Mr. Bakrac:

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my name is Mihajlo Bakrac, attorney-at-law. I'm one of the Defence counsel for the accused Milorad Krnojelac and I shall put a few questions to you now. I would kindly ask you to wait - the presiding Judge has already told you about this - for me to put my question, and then a short time is needed for it to be interpreted, and then you can give your answer. So please do not answer right after I put my question. Sir, do you know a person called Salem Bico?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Salem Bico take part in the fighting in Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got out of the KP Dom, did you give a statement to the security centre in Sarajevo on the 8th of October 1994?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Salem Bico from Gornje Polje?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still claim that you do not know whether Salem Bico took part in the fighting in Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the statement that you gave to the security centre in Sarajevo, that you heard a conversation that the Chetniks, as you called them, were carrying on and they were informing their command Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 that they could not take Gornje Polje because it was being defended by Salem Bico?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't say that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it help you if I would show you the signature on that statement? Could you tell me whether it's yours?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but many things are correct and incorrect because I gave these statements so unwillingly. Either with somebody's help or whatever, at any rate, it was -- what I'm saying now is the truth and this is exactly the way things happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I asked you just now, what I said, you said that you stated that unwillingly or did you not say that at all or did somebody else help you to say something like that? What is true out of all of this?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that I don't remember things correctly. That is to say this was two days after I was released. I was so distraught. I cannot tell you exactly what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since your memory is probably better now, could you tell me, then, whether you did not know about this now and you did know about it two days after you got out of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This situation is not familiar to me because, at that time, I did not know a great many people. I was not a member of any unit. I worked a lot. I did not know about such things at all in relation to questions concerning the SDA party and who did what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's clarify this. Are you saying that this is not your statement or are you saying that this is your statement, but that this was written by somebody else or that somebody else told you to say this? Let's just clarify this, please, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the statement, I refuse this. I did not know many things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, before you proceed, could you tell me what this is relevant to?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, certain persons are mentioned in the case of other witnesses, persons who are treated as civilians in this trial, and then we get this information that they are soldiers. That is the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You're not just cross-examining him because he said something now which is inconsistent with his statement then. It's not a matter going to credit ?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a statement that was given to us, and that is something that the witness started talking about, and then the KP Dom was moved on to immediately. That's the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You say he gave some evidence about this man in his evidence-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, he did not mention that during the examination-in-chief, but that is within the framework of the statement that he had made earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We're not concerned with the statement he made earlier. If you think that his idea of what Mr. Bico did is relevant to your case in some way, you are entitled to cross-examine him on it, but if you want to go to his statement just to try to get him into conflict with what he said in his statement then say we shouldn't believe his evidence generally, you are treading on very irrelevant material. It really doesn't help us. If you can get him into conflict in some way with the evidence he has told us of, certainly, but if you want to prove something to support your case, you are entitled to do it. And if he doesn't come up to what he says in his statement, you may point out that he did say that in his statement. That's all right. But it's got to be relevant in some way to your case and not to his credit. Do you see the distinction?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but with due respect, the Defence believes that the credibility of this witness could be challenged if he is evading questions and giving different answers, that which does not work in favour of the Prosecution and the indictment. That is why this Defence counsel, in his modest opinion, believes that there are things he has said that he is denying now and that is what we wished to ascertain in the case of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Your claim of modesty is rejected, Mr. Bakrac. But quite apart from that, we are not concerned with terribly peripheral issues of inconsistencies between evidence and what was in his statement. Now, that is something I have said all along in this trial. If the material that is in his statement supports -- and which has not been brought up in his evidence-in-chief, nevertheless supports your case, you are entitled to have him agree that that is what he said. And if he does not agree that that is what he has said, you are entitled to investigate how it came to be said in the statement. But it is important that the issue to which you go in his statement is something which supports your case. Now, you've told us that this is to demonstrate that Mr. Bico was not a civilian. And if that is so, and Mr. Bico has been referred to by the witnesses as a civilian, then you are entitled to go into it. But please don't go trawling through his statements just to find out something that you could ask him about and then get him into conflict with what he said in his statement and then say to us we shouldn't believe his evidence, because that is something so peripheral to anything that we have to determine in this case that we have had too much time spent on it already. Now, if we understand each other on that, I'll let you have your head, modestly or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was reprimanded during my very first question, and believe me, there are two or three questions only related to this statement. Please bear in mind that this witness was found last week, practically, that we did not have any information about him whatsoever. In order to speed up the trial, we were ready to hear him immediately, to cross-examine him, and every detail that we have in order to check his credibility is significant for the Defence. Those are the reasons why I wanted to raise certain issues with him, but believe me, with all due respect, please do not be afraid of this. This is only two -- one of the two or three questions we have in relation to the statement he made to the security centre earlier on, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, we are very grateful to you for having cooperated in the way you did, and we will allow you some latitude. A rather seductive appeal of there being only two or three questions suggests that we should let you have your head because it will save time, but do, please, exercise a little bit of restraint as to the extent to which you go into this particular matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's clarify this: You never said this or did you say it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just -- sorry to interrupt the proceedings here, but perhaps if the particular section of the statement be put to him as to what he did say and what he didn't say. It hasn't been put to him at this stage so it's unclear as to what this witness would be actually agreeing to or not. In fact, the witness has said that he doesn't know that Salem Bico was defending the area but the statement refers to the fact that he heard over the radio that Salem Bico may have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that's fair. If you want to challenge something in his statement, you are under an obligation to put to him what it is he has signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all of this was done in order to speed matters up, so I'm going to read only one sentence which is in context. This is on page 2 of his statement in the B/C/S version. It is the second line on this page. "At that moment, I heard that Chetniks were conversing via radio from Gornje Polje and saying that they -- to the command that they could not take Gornje Polje because it is being defended by Salem Bico."

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that. I did sign this but I do not remember this. You have to understand me; I came there distraught, in terrible shape. Maybe many things were added to what I was supposed to sign and I didn't know what I was signing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, we are going to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps this would be a good moment to take a break. From this corner, it seems to be 11.00, to me. I mean the way I see the clock to seems to be exactly 11 .00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It seems we are in a very small courtroom, and you have a poor angle of vision, but we'll take the break even though it may be minute and a half early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked, sir, about some people in the KP Dom whom you had seen, Muslims, the prisoners. Do you know Haso Selimovic, also known as Spona?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was beaten before he arrived at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the warehouse at Livade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he brought to the KP Dom already beaten up?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Nail Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that this person had been taken out of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was he taken away from the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly because they were taken in groups. I cannot tell you the date when he was taken away. He was taken away for an exchange but when, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the group which was called plum pickers which was taken away for an exchange?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of Muhidin Bibovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but he didn't leave with that group of plum pickers. He left to be exchanged much earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that he was alive in America?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is in Germany, in Munich.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I will now come back to the statement you gave to the security centre of Sarajevo. I will read from page 4 very slowly. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 "Around the 20th August 1992, a group of 12 people went for an exchange to Gorazde. However, the exchange did not take place. Today, on the 17th of September 1992, a group of prisoners left allegedly to pick plums. We later called them plum pickers. This group never returned. It seems to me that Muhidin Bibovic was in that group, and I heard that he had allegedly been heard from the States." Now, you are claiming that Muhidin Bibovic had not been in that group, and in 1994, just after your release from the KP Dom, you said that he was in that group and that he had been heard from America?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muhidin Bibovic did not go to pick plums because he left from the mechanic's shop sometime in August 1992. For an exchange from my room, Rasim Kajgana was the only one who was in the group of plum pickers. I know about him because he was in charge of our room. And as for Muhidin Bibovic, I maintain that he left from the mechanic's shop because he worked there as a locksmith and that's his regular occupation, and he didn't go to pick plums because he is alive and he is in Munich today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say he didn't go to pick plums because he is alive and he is in Germany. Is that your prejudice that anyone who left to pick plums is no longer alive?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Muhidin Bibovic did not go to pick plums. Maybe errors were made in the statements given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that now, after 10 years, your memory is better than in 1994 just two years after the events?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know exactly how things happened at the time, and I'm not sure that I made this statement that way, but I do know that I signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, while we are discussing your memory, I will now ask you: Yesterday, during the examination-in-chief, you said that when you brought in a radio into the KP Dom, Burilo came into your Room 16 and took you outside the isolation cell, beat you up, and threw you into the isolation cell; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true that just four days earlier, on Thursday and Friday, you talked with investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor about the subject of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you told the investigators of the OTP that the guard, Burilo, in this incident with the radio, took you to Savo Todovic who told you that it was not allowed to bring a radio into the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because he took away the radio from me, he beat me up, and then he told me what rules existed in the KP Dom. I was not taken to Savo Todovic at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's not true that you said this to the investigators of the OTP, the persons with whom you talked four days ago. I will read out to you now the information we have about what you have said. That you were taken by Burilo to Savo Todovic who told you that it was not allowed to possess a radio at the KP Dom. And then, taking you away from Savo Todovic, Burilo brought you to the cell. So this information conveyed to us is not true, is it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be an error, but I was not taken -- that was outside Room 16 where I was. The isolation cell is on the right-hand side from that room, and everything happened in that hallway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you: Did you say first that you went to Savo Todovic and that Savo Todovic told you it was forbidden and then Burilo took you away? I didn't ask you where the rooms were and where the isolation cells were.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't taken anywhere outside the corridor outside my room, and that's where Burilo took away the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's not true that you saw Savo Todovic on that occasion and that he told you it was forbidden to own a radio?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will stick to the subject of your memory, sir. You said during your examination-in-chief that you never spoke to Juso Dzamalija and you don't know why he was beaten. In the statement you gave to the Prosecutor's office, at least according to the information that we have, you said that Juso Dzamalija had been beaten because his son had been commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His son was not a commander of the military police. He was the commander of the civilian police force, meaning before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you tell us that yesterday during your examination-in-chief? So you did say this to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe we didn't understand each other well. His son had been a police commander before the war. It was called militia then and it's called the police now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said yesterday, regarding this incident, that you don't know what kind of car drove into the compound. Is it true that you told the investigators of the Prosecutor's office that it was a car of the military police which entered the compound, or isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was locked up inside which means I don't know whether it was a civilian vehicle or it was a military police vehicle. I didn't know where that car in the compound -- to whom it belonged because nothing was written on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you said this just four days ago to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor, and now you are not sure you really know what is actually true? Is it true that you told the investigators of the OTP that you knew what the vehicle was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember about the car. I was very frightened. It all happened very quickly. And I don't know where it went. All I know that three of us were there loading something, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you can't remember. You mean you can't remember what happened four days ago? You were frightened. Are you frightened now?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the very thought of the KP Dom makes me frightened. Here in the Court, I'm okay, but if I go back to that in my mind, I can't remember that car, whether it was a civilian vehicle or a police vehicle. I don't know what kind of car it was that took him away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, you are coming in before the end of the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, but I always have this complex that I am slowing down the proceedings and that's possibly why I am making this mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please tell me precisely, loud and clear, did you tell investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor, or whoever it was you talked to, that you know to whom the vehicle belonged, or didn't you say this at all?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know to whom the vehicle belonged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question. I'm not asking you whether you know to whom the vehicle belonged. I'm asking you: Do you remember saying this to the Office of the Prosecutor or you never said it at all?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that a car drove in because we just took him out of the isolation cell and down the stairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to misunderstand me or what? I'm asking you: Did you, four days ago, speaking to investigators of the OTP, say that it was a military vehicle? I'm not asking you now whether it was really a military vehicle or not. I'm asking you did you say this to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That was my question. I am still on the subject of your memory. Did you tell the Office of the Prosecutor four days ago that between the first incident and your incarceration in the isolation cell and the second incident and your incarceration in the isolation cell, there was a gap of two weeks? You told us here it was a month. Compared to the statement you gave four days ago, it is a discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't remember about the timing because it was a period where we didn't even know what the day of the week was, and we didn't measure intervals. Everything I talked about happened from May to the beginning of October. About all of these things that happened, we don't remember exact dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you, did you tell the Office of the Prosecutor that between those two incidents and your incarceration in the cell, there was an interval of two weeks?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm repeating that the interval could have been two weeks or a month. I cannot claim anything to a day because I don't know, myself, how much time passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just interject here. This meeting with the witness is not recorded in the statement format, it is recorded in notes, and this is a summary of the notes that were provided to Defence counsel. He stated -- in those notes, it's recorded that the time difference between the two beatings was "about two weeks," and I think in his testimony he said "about a month," so it's not in absolute terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I would have thought that there wasn't very much importance in this anyway, but it shows the problem of having notes instead of a statement. You proceed, Mr. Bakrac. I hope you've got a better one than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't see any more, but what we have, I, of course, wish we could have that material. But we are hearing a witness here who is supposed to remember what happened nine years ago. I believe that this is a good way of determining his credibility, that is, to what extent he is able to remember things, to what extent he wishes to remember things. So I will continue trying to clear up these details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So about this second incident, you don't know which of the guards beat you; is that true?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you don't know who beat you or is it true that you don't know who beat you [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I don't know the names of the guards. We all call them by nicknames, I don't know their real names, and that's why I'm not mentioning them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say to the Office of the Prosecutor that regarding that second incident when you took two meals at supper, the guard was Maric, also known as Mara, and that you were beat up with two soldiers wearing insignia RS which is supposed to mean the Republika Srpska and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is sorry, we didn't hear the last part of the question.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who beat us and I'm not using real names for that reason. I know about the nickname Mara and I don't know the man's real name. It's true that two soldiers beat me, wearing a big emblem RS which is the sign of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the interpreters did not get the whole of your previous question. Are you able to see it in the transcript there or would you like me to read it to you and have it translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I'll clear this up Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 through questions, through my next question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that guard Mara beat you or didn't he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the entrance to the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also beaten by two soldiers wearing Republika Srpska signs on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because they were there in the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, please explain to me, you just said that Maric beat you. In your statement which you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor, you said that Maric was present, you also said that Maric had tried to intervene, telling soldiers to stop beating you, but he did not intercede in any physical way. Did you forget over those four days or is it on purpose that you are telling a different story now?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not telling a different story. I'm saying what really happened, what actually happened. He tried to defend me and got up and kicked me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
