utterances.text: He tried to defend you and then he got up and kicked you too. That's not what you said to the Prosecutor. You said he didn't get involved physically. You said he told them to stop beating you, just verbally defending you, that's what you said four days ago to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, but while we were going into the isolation cell, he beat me too and he said, "I hadn't beaten you then."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While he was putting you into the isolation cell, you said he kicked you and he said, "It wasn't me."

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the usual provocation of prisoners in isolation cells.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, I remind you, please wait before you answer, you came in well on top of the interpreters there and it was very difficult for them. Do you have the transcript coming up on the screen before you there? You have on your screen now the transcript as it's being typed. If you could, when you have been asked a question, wait until you see the typing stop, that means the interpretation is finished and you will be free to answer the question. Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you say this four days ago to the Office of the Prosecutor what you're telling us now?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I told all about all that happened, it would take me months. I'm speaking very briefly and that's why I'm omitting things. I'm trying, therefore, to say -- to describe the most tragic things. I cannot describe every blow, otherwise it would take a very long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked specifically who beat you on that occasion and who hit you specifically in that one and only incident.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying it was the military police who beat me. I was beaten by Maric while he was unlocking the isolation cell and putting me inside. He beat me and Jasmin Sudar. We were all covered with blood inside the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You now say Maric, you know it's Maric, and yesterday you said you didn't know who the guard was.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very well who the guards were. I don't know their names that's why I'm not even trying to tell their names. I know their nicknames, Mara, Predo, Busi, I don't know their full names, that's why I'm not telling you who the guards were by name. I don't know their names just as nobody there knew my real name, my full name. They all knew me by (redacted) .

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the witness inadvertently identified himself. Perhaps we should redact this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm trying to protect you through my questions and you have to be careful too because you've asked for protective measures. So you are not sure that it was Maric or you're not sure because you don't know what his name was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sure, because his nickname was Mara and I knew Mara even before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean that before the war, you also knew that his name was Maric?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew his name was Maric even before the war and you knew his nickname was Mara, and yesterday you told us that you didn't want to mention the name of the guards because you didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I maintain with full responsibility that I don't know his full name and surname even today. I know him as Mara and that is true to this day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand, sir, that you are saying one thing now and a second ago you said a different thing? You said you didn't know his name, to this day you don't know it, and now you say you know it and you knew it before the war.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew him as Mara. We knew others as Predo and Busi. We didn't know the names, the real names of any of the guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, this is clear. Will you please tell us about the incident related to Nurko Nisic, the first one in the so-called searching room. How long did the whole thing last, this beating of Nurko Nisic in that room for searches?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly. I was waiting for perhaps five or ten minutes before the guards threw me out into the compound. Nurko stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you entered the compound, did the beating of Nurko Nisic stop?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because I was no longer there and I don't know what happened from then on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you told the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutors, that is the person from the Prosecution office to whom you talked, that the beating lasted about ten minutes and that you were thrown out into the compound when the beating had stopped?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was there for about five or ten minutes, then I entered the compound, which means I don't know whether the beating stopped then because I was no longer there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor that you were pushed into the compound after the beating had stopped?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that. I was thrown in and I don't know what happened after that. At that moment, the guard took the two of us, we passed the two of them who -- and were thrown into the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the first interview you had with the investigators of the OTP over the telephone, did you mention that Atif Jasarevic was present there and 16 other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes these are people who were taken away, who we saw being taken away and returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when Nurko Nisic was beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, Defence counsel asked, "Were they present when Nurko Nisic was beaten?"

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the first interview you had with the investigators of the OTP, did you say that Jasarevic was present there with 16 other persons, present during the beating of Nurko Nisic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which room were you in when Nurko Nisic was beaten on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Room 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that; can you remember?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was mid-May, the month of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked to us about an incident concerning a radio. How did you get the radio into the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked at the hospital with a few other detainees. I got it from a friend who was lying in hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How big was this radio?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a small radio that could fit into your pocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you searched at the entrance into the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My blouse was over my back. I put it on the table for searches and they didn't look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went in and out of the KP Dom, did they register your name somewhere; did they write it down?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because a guard went with us and took us back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he did not register your name anywhere. When you left and when you came back, he didn't enter anything into a book or something?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether such books were kept. As for that, I don't know whether there was something like that further on in the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where the command -- where was this command?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reception hall where they took us from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said when your radio was taken away from you, you said during the examination-in-chief that Burilo said to you that there's no more TV, no more radio, newspapers, et cetera. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was deprived of all liberty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this; in which month?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of this happened mid-May, June. That's when it all happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, you said that you were the only one who was deprived of radio, TV and newspapers from then onwards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was clear to all of us that we were deprived of all possible human rights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said and you repeated just now that the beatings occurred in mid-May and June. What happened after June 1992?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the beatings that took place -- the KP Dom was established on the 17th of April. That evening, I came to the KP Dom. From then onwards, until the 1st of October 1992, that's this period of beatings, taking people out and we didn't know where people were being taken to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just talking about beatings. Did you say that there weren't any more beatings after mid-May and June 1992?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but less. That is to say that all the beatings that took place took place in May, June, July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said July now too. What about after July? Were there any beatings and specifically what did you see or hear in terms of that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will the Court allow me to disassociate myself from dates? The 15th of April, when I was detained in Livade, until the 1st of October, dates of beatings and of taking people away and bringing them back, so I cannot stick only to May and June and to say that that happened only then. I know exactly that there were people taken out and brought back and beaten during those months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, in the examination-in-chief, you said it was May and June when these beatings occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the case of individual persons. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think in his examination-in-chief he also said that beatings occurred up to the 1st of October, in his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you got the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I don't have it on me at the moment but he may have said it a couple of times in his examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you think you are getting very far with this particular point, Mr. Bakrac? You can't really pin him down to dates. I agree that there can be a very wide variation between something which might have happened one month or ten months later, but I don't think that the witness can be expected to remember very precisely this sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I agree. I am satisfied with this answer and I do not intend to ask the witness any further about this particular matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were asked whether the persons who were with you the first time in the isolation cell got any medical treatment from a doctor. Did you seek that from anyone?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but nobody allowed us that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you ask for medical care?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could only ask the guards who, then, took people to lunch and brought them back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you specifically about persons who were with you in the isolation cell, Dervisevic Suad, and the person Zaim and you. That night that you were in the isolation cell, or the next day, did you ask for medical care?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had no one to ask. In addition to that, we were all beaten up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said just now that you had no one to ask and only a moment before that you said that you addressed the guards.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but can you understand while I was there why I had been beaten? If I was not in a party, if I did not have weapons, why was all of that done? Well, it was said quite clearly to me, you did not have weapons, you were not in the party, you are only guilty because you are a Muslim. So what was I supposed to ask for in addition to that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I understand your bitterness now, but that will not help us get to the truth. I asked you whether there was a doctor at the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for us Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There wasn't a medical technician either, a nurse?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat; not for the Muslims. For the Serbs, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that there were numerous witnesses here, several witnesses who got drips, medicines from these same doctors, will you change your opinion?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You said that you were interrogated at the KP Dom and that you were asked whether you had weapons and which party you belonged to.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they find an SDA membership card on you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I did not belong to any party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, during the examination-in-chief, you said that you were asked which party you belonged to and, after that, which role you played in the party. Why would they ask you that if you did not belong to any party?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps it's not a question for the witness to answer why questions are being put by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I agree with you entirely. Mr. Bakrac, where does this get us? I know that you are saying that you only have a certain amount of material, but you agreed to the matter going on. It doesn't really permit you to ask totally inadmissible questions. He has no control over what questions are asked by the Prosecution. Now can you get on to the next point.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. I shall move on, but still, this is not clear to me. The Prosecution put many questions, asking the witness to reach his own conclusions. The witness actually said that he was asked what party he belonged to and what role he had in the party. In my opinion, it is logical that he said that he belonged to the party and that then he was therefore asked which role he had in the party. So it's not for him to say why he was asked that. We are simply trying to find out what he answered in response to that question. I shall move on then, but I thought it was necessary to give this kind of explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Both parties seem to have some belief that the politics of this are important. I have never understood why except perhaps to give some sort of a motive, but it's not necessary to go into that at this stage. If you want to know what it was he said in answer to the question, we'll look it up in the transcript. If you want him to repeat it now to see whether he's got a memory of what he said yesterday, you ask him that. But that's not what your question was. That's not the question to which objection was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said, in relation to the death of Juso Dzamalija that an autopsy was not carried out. How can you know about that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not maintain that an autopsy was not carried out. The body was taken out of the KP Dom and I was returned to the isolation cell, so I don't really know anything about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I shall remind you now, since I have the transcript here, and I didn't want to go and read what the honorable Trial Chamber believes is irrelevant anyway, so I shall read from the transcript. You said -- I haven't got the page here, this is the unredacted text, I'm reading from the transcript, that you cannot answer whether it was suicide or murder because there was no autopsy.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of us, yes, I'm trying to tell you that I did not see anything except that we carried the body out and put it out there. I don't know anything else that happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you don't know that, why did you infer that no autopsy was carried out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how this question was put, but I maintain to you that we could not know anything. We only got him out of the isolation cell. Whether he was taken to be searched further or whatever, I don't know. We just took him out and that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, in connection with the other incident, that you heard that Nurko Nisic was being beaten by a guard and that Nurko Nisic said, or rather that he said to Nurko, "Bosnia is not --" "That is no way to defend Bosnia, Nurko." How can you know this was a guard?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that a guard was beating him because we did not know who was beating him because we were locked up in the room. We just heard moans, beating, we did not know who was doing the beating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any other person in the KP Dom named Nurko?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Nurko Nisic before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How well did you know him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very little.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you know that it was the voice of Nurko Nisic? Did you hear the voice of Nurko Nisic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only knew that because I worked with his brother who is now in Sarajevo. Through him, I knew Nurko. I saw him when they beat him, around 12.00, when he was taken out with some other men in the evening, another time when he was taken for an exchange but I don't know anything else about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are saying to us now that you saw him that night when he was being beaten and you didn't tell us that before. Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the evening, during the day while I was standing at the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the day, at what time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 11.00, 12.00, lunchtime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the evening, when did you hear them beating Nurko Nisic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps after that, because Nurko Nisic, like everybody else, was taken out every day, every evening, for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again you are telling us about a new detail which you've not mentioned at all. How many days and how many evenings did they take Nurko Nisic out for interrogations?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you understand that this taking out went on infinitely and that we don't know how many times people were taken out for interrogations. I know about that day when he was beaten and that evening we were in the room, all of us. That was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm trying to find out how come you know that it was him who they were beating. How do you know it was him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day, yes, in the evening no. We just heard, "Get up Nurko, that's no way to defend Bosnia." Those were the words that one of the guards were saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you know it's a guard?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way we talk. The military police, the guards, never mind, somebody was beating him but we don't know who, we don't know by name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this somebody just say "Nurko" or did this person say "Nurko Nisic"?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, believe me. I know that it's Nurko and Asim Mezbur. Since Nurko was Nisic, I think there was only one. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are not sure whether it was Nurko Nisic or Asim Mezbur?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nurko Nisic is only one, there aren't several of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see from your window the interior of the room from which you could hear these sounds?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We could only see the window from which the sound was coming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in Room 11, if I am not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying now that from that Room 11 you could not see what was going on inside, you could only hear?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You showed us the room, or rather, the window where you heard this from. How could you locate the sound, that it was coming precisely from that window?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a big distance between Room 11 and the administration building. Perhaps it's about 10 or 15 metres. In the room then, we had about 80 men, that is to say that we were all at the window then and we were listening to this, who they were beating, and we heard these words exactly, the words that were uttered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which part of Room 11 were you, in that part which is closer to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 the metalwork shop and the hospital or the room that is closer to the town of Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The room that is closer to the metalwork shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few minutes ago you said to us that in 1992, you did not dare walk up to the window at all. And now you say that 80 of you were standing at the window on that occasion. How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's hard for me to explain that, but if it is a question of beating, we were all there and we were listening and we heard full well what was going on and who was being beaten. If a guard would come, would see us at the window, he would come and throw that person out and take him to an isolation cell, so it's right that we were not allowed to be at the windows, however, it was not necessary to do that. You could sit on the bed and you could hear all of this ideally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were sitting on the beds in your room and you were listening to what was going on in the building opposite to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is not correct that you were at the window?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well let me tell you, out of 100 men, it is not true that you can have all of them at one window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you personally at the window?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sitting on the bed and I was waiting to see who'd be next.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the window open?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Half of the glass was missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the window was closed, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You said that at the KP Dom or, rather, that you were taken by a Black Mariah of the KP Dom to work on Milorad Krnojelac's house. In your interviews with the OTP, did you mention, did you say that you went every morning with the civilian police and that you were escorted by a regular policeman?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We went in a vehicle from the KP Dom with a guard to the building where we worked. The guard would withdraw, Krnojelac's son would stay with us all the time, and he would guard us. That was the time when I was there and when I worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw Krnojelac at the KP Dom. Did you see him in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite a few times, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say to the investigator of the OTP that he often wore civilian clothes and, from time to time, a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true that you stated that you saw Krnojelac mostly during the day, in daytime?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you said that you cannot remember that you saw him in the evening at all?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see him in the evening hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you mentioned, in your interviews with the Office of the Prosecutor, the president of the Court in relation to a certain group of people?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the court-martial, yes, that's true, and all the questions went through that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, so all the examinations went through the unit of the president of the court-martial, if my understanding is correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we called it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At my interrogations, Zoran Vladicic was present and Vojo Starovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two of them were there when I was being interrogated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they the representatives of the court-martial?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly. All the interrogations took place there with them, so I cannot tell you exactly because all the interrogations went through them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you saw personally the person who you claim was the president of the court-martial.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we knew each other very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Tell me, please, did you say in your statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor and in your interviews with investigators of the OTP that Savo Todovic was a person who gave work assignments and who designated punishments for prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we say "prisoners," do you mean detainees of Muslim nationality?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that on one occasion it was Mr. Krnojelac who drove you to the house. Which car did he drive you in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I'm not sure but I think it was a red Yugo. I cannot remember the car very well, but I think it was a small car, a Yugo

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said during your examination-in-chief that you saw some bodies in the Drina River and you showed us on that map the place, the islet where you saw them. How far is that from the bridge in front of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 50 and 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like first of all to get your permission to seek clarification about the photo documentation which we said we would be using. For the purposes of questioning, we identified this photo documentation as ID D1, so other evidence will get identification numbers in sequence, and we have two sets of photographs. The first set is linked with the KP Dom. We identified it as A and each photograph was identified as A1, A2, A3 and so on. And the second set of photographs relates to the house of the accused Krnojelac. We identified it as the B series, and each photograph will be marked B1, B2 and so on. With the help of the usher, I will show this to the witness, and this photograph is identified as ID D1/A29 in the potential evidence presented by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure where the D comes from. You said we had two sets of photographs, one with the letter A and various numbers and the other with the letter B and various numbers. You've now talked about D1/A29. Where's the D from?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you will excuse me, in our system, we don't use this system of marking. We were just trying to give an identification number to avoid confusion and we added D for Defence to know that it is the Defence material. So it's ID D1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But eventually it will have to become an exhibit and it will then be given the letter D, just as the Prosecution's have P, so let us just call it for the moment ID 1/A29, and then when it becomes an exhibit, it will become D1/A29. Is that satisfactory?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, apparently --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, it is. I think there is just a mistake in the interpretation. I can show you on the photo document itself how we marked it. IDD, identification number Defence. Not just ID, it's IDD to distinguish from the Prosecution's numbers, to avoid confusion. That was the only intent of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, that is now clear. Now what do you want to say, Mr. Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to be involved in the way that you mark the exhibits, but apparently there is a D1 in evidence already, I've been advised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, well, I've noticed that we are up to D3 already, but this is their IDD number and then when it becomes an exhibit, it will become, hopefully, D3 1/A29. No, I'm sorry, D3/A29. Yes, do proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if this creates confusion, we can leave only ID without the additional D. Let's clarify it for the future. I thought this was easy, but if you don't think so, we could do it differently. I thought we just wanted to distinguish between the Prosecution and the Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I agree with what you propose. Your documents will be marked with an identifying number, preceded by the letters "IDD" for defendant's identification number. When it becomes an exhibit, it will have to take its place in the line. You've already got D1 and a D2, so this will become D3/A29.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you got the photograph? I don't know whether the Prosecution's got those photographs, do they? Are we ever going to see them?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution has these photographs. We've already given them. I would like to ask the usher to take the lower photograph, A29, and put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, will you please look at this photograph and tell me: Is this the islet which you referred to which could be seen from the bridge?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I cannot find my way around this picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember whether this is the islet which you showed us on the map?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question precisely. I'm confused by the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You will remember, Mr. Bakrac, that the witness pointed on the map some distance past the KP Dom flowing downstream despite the fact that it was described going up the map. It was some distance downstream from the KP Dom at a place where the river seems to have a slight bend. Now, whether that was near a bridge or not, we don't know. Have you got a photograph without the bridge obscuring it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have any photographs which could show that. We will bring an investigator who will explain this. I said that we do have a photo documentation to present to the witnesses, but this is the part downstream. I would only like the witness to answer, if he possibly can, if he agrees that left -- to the left side of this islet, the Drina River is deeper?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know, and you lived in Foca, are there any other bridges above this bridge in the upper flow of the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are three bridges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Foca itself?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true that beyond the bridge which is opposite the KP Dom and which we referred to here, the Cehotina river flows into the Drina?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many bridges there are on the Cehotina river on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 the territory of Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two bridges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in the upper part of the flow of the Cehotina and the Drina rivers, that is beyond the bridge outside the KP Dom on the territory of the Foca town itself, there are another five bridges?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said that above this bridge near the KP Dom, in the upper flow of the Drina River, there are another three bridges and there are two on the Cehotina river; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The one at the KP Dom, the one in the centre, and one at Brod, those are the three bridges on the Drina. There are two bridges on the Cehotina; Aladza, one, and the second one at Donje Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So beyond this bridge, there are another two bridges on the Drina and two on the Cehotina, in the upper part of the flow, before this bridge at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all the four bridges above this KP Dom bridge are on the territory of Foca town?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also in the upper flow of the Drina River and outside the KP Dom, there are other bridges; is that true?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There exists one at Brod and one at the railway administration. The bridge which leads to Tjentiste and one at the railway administration which separates the intersection between Tjentiste and Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all of these bridges are in the upper flow of the Drina and the last in the line is the bridge near the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Is it correct, sir, you told us here regarding the conduct of Mr. Krnojelac that he was good, and that he acted naturally, normally. Is it true that you said to the Office of the Prosecutor that, while you were working at Krnojelac's house, he acted in a friendly manner towards you and all the others from the KP Dom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask for the assistance of the usher in showing from the photo documentation of the Defence --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, from the photo documentation of the Defence, we'd like to show photograph B1. I would like this photograph to be put closer, if possible, zoomed. No, not that much, sorry. Is this Milorad Krnojelac's house where you worked?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, I would like to show the witness the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The photograph is marked B4. If possible, please zoom it a little. Thank you. Is this a photograph depicting the back side of the house which you previously identified as Milorad Krnojelac's house on which you worked?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not sure?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the top of this photograph, below the roof, can you see black traces of fire, flame?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Below the roof, in the right-hand part and in the middle, around the door and the windows, can you see traces of black soot?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the walls were half destroyed and you had to rebuild the rest. Here, we see that burnt walls remained standing up to the roof.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the inner walls, the partition walls were destroyed, whereas the outer walls remained standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, I remind you, wait for that typing on the screen ahead of you to stop before you answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. With the assistance of the usher, I would like to show the witness the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is photograph B6. Is this the interior of Milorad Krnojelac's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next photograph, please, B7. Is this the interior of Milorad Krnojelac's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next photograph, please. Is this the interior of Milorad Krnojelac's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The photograph is marked B8. Can I have photograph B9, please, with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the interior of Milorad Krnojelac's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to show us the last two photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This photograph B10, does it also show the interior of the house of Milorad Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I also have B11, please. Is this photograph also one of the interior of Milorad Krnojelac's house on which you worked?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain what had been done on the walls?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Scraping off of the plaster and preparation for wall painting, cleaning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean to tell us that the plaster on these walls is new?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it hadn't been done yet. We were just scraping the old one to make the walls bare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see any electrical or water supply installations in these walls?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. We won't need these photographs any more. Can you please tell us, you talked about the food at the KP Dom and you said that in 1993 when the warden was replaced, the food improved. Is it true that in the statement you gave to the security centre you said that the suffering regarding food lasted for the first 15 months-- sorry, eight months?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that the food improved after five months -- eight months, beginning with the date of your incarceration?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, starting with May, the food got better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you will agree that at that time, Milorad Krnojelac was still warden after eight months of your detention?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you exact details how long Krnojelac was warden because I didn't work in the administration then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you, is it true that eight months into your detention, the food improved?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the work group which worked outside, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said just now that in 1993, the food improved?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the middle of 1993, and the entire 1994 was good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's not true what you said, that eight months into your detention, the food was bad. It's not true what you said to the security centre of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The food was not bad, it was horrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get eggs?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but very, very rarely. One egg per person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get meat?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get milk?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rare occurrence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a general shortage of food in town?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that from the very beginning, you worked in the metalwork shop. Is it true what you said during your examination-in-chief, that although you worked every day in the metalwork shop, you never had a bath in the whole of 1992?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't work only in the metalwork shop, I worked everywhere and I did all kinds of jobs. I could heat water for myself where other people couldn't. Later, I obtained water in canisters. I could get hold of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you could have a bath, whereas others -- you could take a bath, other people couldn't, and now you are saying that you heated water for others in canisters. For what did you heat it then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The boiler room didn't work then. The central heating didn't work then. The showers downstairs didn't work. All of it was destroyed. People had nowhere to take a bath, to wash.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So due to these reasons, you couldn't take a shower - it was destroyed - but you made due, and you did wash. You heated water and you took a bath.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You claim that your bed sheets were not changed during the whole of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you wash them yourself?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And even that bed linen, it wasn't washed all that year?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because we slept on blankets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had no white sheets, no linen?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All that was left over from the former KP Dom civilians who were regulars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And my last question: Do you know a person by the name of Atif Jasarevic, and did he work together with you on Milorad Krnojelac's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, the Defence has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No re-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. That concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to give it. You are now free.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I just have a couple of questions, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, we'll deal with them at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25 Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I just have a few questions in relation to the photographs that have been identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It was two questions before but it's a few now, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I should have kept it broader earlier. Perhaps if the usher could put the photograph IDD-1B1 on the overhead, thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Smith:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you -- you said to my learned friend that you recognised this house as the house of Milorad Krnojelac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last day that you worked on the house, did it look in the same state that it is on this photograph or are there some changes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were some changes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you can point out on the photograph the changes that have been made to the house since you worked there.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The roof construction had not been made, and I do not remember this part having been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The witness indicates the roof of the house that's white when he referred to roof construction, and then he indicated the building with orange bricks as the one he didn't remember being there at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the tiles -- were any tiles on the roof when you left on your last day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had the wood work on the roof, had that been placed on the house, on which the tiles are resting, on the last day that you were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The construction had just been placed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the detainees put that construction, that roof construction on?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just to be clear, there were no tiles on the roof; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just -- that is a little bit ambiguous. Were there tiles on the roof when you left on your last day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look on the photograph on the -- it looks to be the second floor of the house, or the floor above the ground floor, on the left-hand side there's wood work in the doorways of the house. Was that wood work there when you left?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think you said that you can't remember whether the house construction with the orange bricks was there when you worked on the house.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the tiles being placed on the roof since you worked at the house, are there any other extra additions that have been made to the outside of the house - this is the white house - since you worked on it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's how the house looked when you left it on the last day, apart from the roof?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this part, which is new and made of bricks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many floors were there in Mr. Krnojelac's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was the ground floor down there, and then the upstairs; there were two stories up there and there was the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the ground, was there a cafe there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what work was done by the detainees in the cafe area?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cleaning was done, iron steps were made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the iron steps, where were they to go to? Were they to go to the first and second floors or were they just simply steps for the cafe?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ground floor and the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If the witness can be shown photograph B8 and B9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you recognised this staircase, the black staircase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Did he ever refer to B8? I thought that he was asked about B9.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I have that he referred to B8, Your Honour, but I may have mistakenly noted it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you really want me to tell you the truth, Your Honour, honestly I don't remember. But at any rate, I shall avail myself of this opportunity to object. If we showed the photograph, we have to say whether this is the indoors of that house, not asking him whether he recognises the staircase, so I think that my learned friend put the question the wrong way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the distinction. He's asking him whether he identifies this staircase as the staircase in the house in which he worked. That's identifying the inside of the house, I would have thought myself. But my recollection is that that was shown to him by the usher and was then moved up to show B9. I've just been told it's in the transcript as B8, so I'm sorry to have interfered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I'll clarify it anyway, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how many staircases were made for the house, for Krnojelac's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there while the work on the ground floor was being done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how many staircases -- was one staircase made or two made for the house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I worked in the ground floor, I'm not sure about the upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you recognise this particular room in the house. Is that upstairs or is it downstairs, on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upstairs, the first floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps if we look at photograph B9. You said also that you recognised this staircase. Is that right, you recognise that staircase as well?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour do you remember the staircase being, or the staircase or staircases that were made?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A basic red colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first staircase that was shown to you was a black staircase, so are you sure whether that was made for the house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an old staircase and the new one that was painted red, should have been the new one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the staircase on photograph B9?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at this photograph, is this the way you remembered the room when you left?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has any further work been done on that room since you've left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How can he say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, from the photograph, I omitted to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He's just said that's how he remembers the house when he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Your Honour, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you look at B8, the photograph on top again. You said that you recognised that room. Has any further work been done in that room since you left, sorry from -- does it look the same as when you left as in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is hard for me to orient myself because I spent 10 days there, doing the cleaning. That is a very brief period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it the case that you can't specifically recognise this particular room; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With great difficulty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were working on the house, was there a large amount of construction material there that -- similar to what appears on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown photograph B11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you stated that you recognised this photograph as a room in the house.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe in more detail what was done in relation to the walls? You said that some work was done on the walls.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the roof construction had not been placed, that is to say, it wasn't covered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the wood work was there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to the walls, did you or other detainees do any work on these particular walls?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Scraping the walls, yes. The rest, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this room in the photograph look the same as when you left the house when you worked on the last day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You mean other than the roof?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct. Other than the roof, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, without the roof, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in summary, can you just restate what work was done on the house, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staircase, the roofing, the roof construction. I can't tell you more than that. I don't know what was done. I know what I was doing, and I know about part of the staircase while that was being made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you finished on the last day at the house, did you know whether detainees worked at that house after your last day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know how long they worked on the house for, about how many days?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, once again, sir, thank you for giving your evidence. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, and good bye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is actually -- this was the last Prosecution witness, but we have three outstanding matters. The first matter you probably recall, that in relation to the testimony of Mr. Masovic, Mr. Masovic got the task to add additional information on the list of detainees who were last seen in the KP Dom. And Mr. Masovic has actually achieved his goal and he has made this list, but since this morning, we are trying to get it over through fax and we were not very successful. It's actually 39 pages that have to be faxed and we couldn't get Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 it yet. It has to be done in intervals because of the bad lines and it's not completely here now. Actually, only the beginning is here. So we cannot provide this list right now, and before closing this case, we would have to ask to get an opportunity to hand it in later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, we'd better wait until you've dealt with the other two matters that you want to raise but there would be nothing wrong, that I could see, with you saying that you close your case subject to the production of that document when it arrives. I think we've got to have a final statement that the Prosecution case is otherwise closed, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So that's all right. When do you expect to be able to get the whole document?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We hope to get it during this day, but tomorrow at the latest. But I'm not really sure because I haven't seen anything of it. I do not know if it is in the B/C/S language, but I very much think so. So we would also have to produce a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, there will be no problem, I should think, with that even if it doesn't come until next week sometime. There would be no need for us to even re-assemble for you to formally tender it, provided that you have otherwise closed your case, subject to the production of that and an English translation, and that can be done informally.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I was just informed that the document is in the English language so we would only need the fax to get through today or tomorrow morning. The other issue in relation to Mr. Masovic's testimony was the question of the ICRC list that he received on the particular meeting, and actually, we had asked the ICRC three questions in relation to this list, and we had asked them in a letter dated 23rd March 2001, first on the basis of the Trial Chamber's request to the Prosecution, could you provide, firstly, confirmation that the copy of this document was provided by the ICRC to the various former parties to the conflict at a working group meeting during or after 1996. Secondly, information as to whether the ICRC compiled this particular document or whether it was received from another source. And thirdly, the general source of the information on the document, whether compiled by the ICRC or not. And yesterday, we received a fax from the ICRC. They -- I don't want to read it here, out fully, but the last sentence is the following: "For the above reasons, I regret to inform you that we cannot provide the additional information requested in your letter."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Not even the confirmation that that was the document handed out to people?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Nothing at all. And we would like to enter both documents into evidence, that is, our letter and the response from the ICRC, and we have actually provided it to the Defence counsel already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: They make it very hard for people to like them, I'm afraid, the ICRC, at times. You see, they don't even deal with the first matter that you have asked. One can understand, if not agree with, their desire to avoid disclosing the source of the information used to compile the document, but it seems to me to be being recalcitrant to their interests to refuse even to confirm that the document was handed to the various parties in that working group. However, that's what we face. Yes, well, now, Mr. Bakrac, do you object to the tender of this material?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit P451. It's a matter which, of course, will, I suppose, go to the weight to be afforded to Mr. Masovic's evidence, but there's nothing that you can do to cure it and I think that from the point of view of the Tribunal, it's regrettable. The other material, well, even if you took the view which I expressed in the ICRC decision in the Simic case, I don't think that we could require them to produce that information. It is of importance but not of such an overwhelming importance that they should have to reveal confidential sources. The Prosecution case is based upon a system which was operating and the mere fact that it came from the ICRC, if we accept Mr. Masovic's evidence, would be of some value or some probative value of the material provided. It's just that we can't test it any further. So I think that we should put the ICRC to one side now that you have produced this material. So that's the second matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And the third matter relates to the expert report of the Prosecution expert, but Ms. Kuo, who has actually dealt with the matter, will speak to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have submitted the 13-page report for formal translation, which is not yet available, but we have had a very cursory oral summary of it and, based on that, we understand that our expert concludes that Mr. Krnojelac was perfectly normal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you have to enlighten us as to what the Defence expert says, because we haven't -- all we know was that it was a psychiatric or psychological examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: We don't -- we still don't have a copy of that in English and we haven't been able to get that summarised, but based on what the Prosecution expert says, we understand that their disagreement, there is a slight disagreement that the Defence expert thinks -- concludes that Mr. Krnojelac was more subject to anxiety than other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is this a matter of mitigation, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: It's not exactly clear because we haven't had the full discussion about the relevance. So at this point, based on what we understand, the Prosecution is not inclined to put this report in its case in chief because we believe there is no issue in dispute. And we don't want to take on the burden of having to produce evidence that an accused is normal because we think that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that's assumed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't think there can be any doubt about that. If the -- if an accused person wants to raise an issue as to his mental responsibility, the onus is on him to do so. But let's see what the accused says, or at least his counsel says, is the issue that it goes to and then we can come back and see what you have to do with your reply.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, does this go to some question of his mental responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, our client is not defending himself by claiming mental irresponsibility or mental disorders of any kind. We asked for neuropsychiatric expertise and the experts were instructed to see how the accused behaves in certain situations. Yesterday, last night, I got the expert opinion from the Prosecutor's expert and I had to deal with the witness we had today, so I didn't really have time to deal at any length with this, and we expect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: May I interrupt you. To what issue would you be tendering your report? Forget the Prosecution report. Do you propose to tender your report?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we shall intend to tender it and we shall also call the expert to explain what the expert found with regard to all of those matters that were the subject of the expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, I wonder if you could just answer the question I keep on wanting to know the answer to. To what issue does this go? Is it a matter in mitigation or is it a matter that goes to his criminal responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, not his criminal responsibility. In our pre-trial brief, we already said which path the Defence would take. So this could possibly work in terms of determination of guilt. This expertise would therefore relate to mitigation, mitigating circumstances, actually, not criminal responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's what I thought, but I just wanted you to say so. But thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Well, Ms. Kuo, if it goes in mitigation, that's a matter upon which the accused bears the onus of proof and therefore, it would be normal for you to tender it in reply.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And if we have the opportunity -- let me ask for clarification. Do you mean that we should wait until their report is put in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes. If we have the opportunity in rebuttal, that was what we were concerned about. Then if that's the case -- and also we may wish to use this during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Of course, of course. You will give a copy to everybody -- well, you've already given Mr. Bakrac a copy which he can read and we can't. There is a lot of law in some common law countries about the obligation of the Prosecution to tender the whole of its case on guilt in the case in chief if it knows of any particular issue which is being raised. That's usually considered in the light of the fact that they are jury trials and that appellate courts have a passionate belief that juries are swayed by what happens at the last moment in the case. I don't think it applies in the Tribunal's proceedings. The Rules provide for cases in reply and then rebuttal. I think they call them something quite a little different, but that's the way I look at it. So that this is a matter where the defendant bears an onus of proof. They are going to tender it in their case, so the Prosecution can, if it wishes to, tender it in reply and call the witness, the expert witness if necessary. Well, does that satisfy the last of your queries?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right then. Well, then, may we take it that the Prosecution is now closed, subject to the production of the annotated list that Mr. Masovic is working on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the Prosecution would rest then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. Well, Mr. Bakrac, you understand that the Prosecution case has closed. They can't lead anything else, but they will be producing that document which you sought from Mr. Masovic when it is finally here and there is a translation made of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The Defence really has no reason to create a problem in this respect. So far, we've had a perfectly satisfactory cooperation with the Office of the Prosecutor. I believe the Defence can wait, and I hope we'll have enough time to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I think you'll probably find that you'll get it next week some time, but you don't want them to have the Trial Chamber re-assembled in order to tender it. It can be done on an informal basis and confirmed when we do re-assemble for the pre-Defence conference. Are you satisfied with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I am very grateful to you. We are grateful to both parties for the cooperation that has occurred during the course of this trial. It has certainly speeded the matter up without anybody losing any advantages or rights. Well, in those circumstances, we will re-assemble on Thursday, the 26th of April for the pre-Defence conference and we expect the Defence case to commence on the 1st of May. Is there anything anybody else wants to raise at this stage? Very well, we shall see you again at the end of April. I hope you all have a happy Serbian -- orthodox and non-orthodox Easter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: at 3.05 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday the 26th day of April, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
